clue.text: The next people seen on television

definitions.meaning: the people living next door to you
the long-running Australian TV soap opera of that name

explanation.surface: A teaser asking which people are coming up next on the TV schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: The folk next door are your neighbours, and Neighbours is also an Australian soap opera popular on British television.

clue.text: Every one is English and a good companion

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order awarded for good service

explanation.surface: A claim that every single Englishman makes fine company.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the post-nominal letters of a Companion of Honour, a British honour; 'good' nods to the distinction it rewards.
explanation.definitionFit: Each refers to every individual in a group, taken one at a time.

clue.text: Collect up scrap around the place

indicators.note: around tells us the reversed scrap encloses the next word
in a down entry, up means the word for scrap is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy away bits of rubbish strewn about the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAG into GAR, which goes 'around' THE; 'place' merely rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather things is to bring them together into one spot, a synonym of collecting.

clue.text: From an Irishman, that's flattery!

parts.note: the smooth persuasive talk said to come from kissing a famous stone in County Cork, Ireland

explanation.surface: An exclamation at the charming compliments paid by an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: Kissing the stone at a castle in County Cork is said to grant the gift of the gab.
explanation.definitionFit: Blarney is a word for flattering, cajoling talk, associated with Irish charm.

clue.text: Press gets no initial increase of power

indicators.note: the word for an increase of power is to lose its opening letter

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rise in electrical power

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about failing to get an early boost in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like the newspapers but is a verb meaning to push or urge.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone is to push them hard to act, a synonym of urging.

clue.text: Place is designed to be distinctive

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters of the words before it have been purposely arranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: A remark that a venue has been built to stand out from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges the letters of PLACE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something special is out of the ordinary, marked out from others.

clue.text: A vulgar ailment

parts.note: vulgar in its old sense of ordinary or widespread among the people, describing an everyday sniffle

explanation.surface: A mention of some coarse, unmentionable illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vulgar' suggests rudeness, but its older meaning is ordinary or widespread, describing the most frequent of minor illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday viral infection of nose and throat is ordinary, that is vulgar in the old sense.

clue.text: He's a flaming nutter!

parts.note: flaming as both a mild curse and literally involving fire, describing someone with a mania for starting fires

explanation.surface: An exasperated outburst about a man who is completely mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flaming' reads as a British intensifier, like 'bloody', but here means literally burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyromaniac has a compulsive urge to set fires, a madness of the flames.

clue.text: Pass a swimmer

definitions.meaning: to go past, as a verb phrase
a small spiny-finned fish of coastal waters

explanation.surface: A request to let a swimmer overtake in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by is to move past something, and a goby is a small sea fish.

clue.text: This corner's not right

parts.note: a corner where two lines meet at less than ninety degrees, so not a right one

explanation.surface: A complaint that a room's corner has been built wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' sounds like a fault, but it means the angle is not ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry names an angle under ninety degrees acute, as opposed to a right angle.

clue.text: Game played in clubs by a tough guy

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
Rambo is the muscular action-film hero played by Sylvester Stallone

explanation.surface: A sport played at nightclubs by a hard man.
explanation.walkthrough: Crambo is an old rhyming word game.
explanation.definitionFit: Crambo is a parlour game in which players find rhymes for a given word.

clue.text: Cut one's hrt prescription

indicators.note: a prescription is something made up to order, so the letters are made up anew

parts.note: taken as written, the S counting as a letter
taken as written, the letters of hormone replacement therapy

explanation.surface: Someone reducing their dose of hormone replacement therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prescription' rearranges ONES and HRT; HRT is hormone replacement therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something is to reduce its length or duration.

clue.text: Sedate aspects of a serious man

parts.note: sober means calm and sedate
sides are aspects of a matter

explanation.surface: Describing the calm facets of a grave fellow's character.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobersides is a humourless, staid person.

clue.text: Hopeful of sight, I'm first for implant

indicators.note: for implant tells us the following pieces are set into the word for of sight

parts.note: optic means relating to the eye or vision
taken as written without the apostrophe
1st written with I for the figure one

explanation.surface: An eye patient hoping to be first in line for a lens implant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for implant' puts IMIST inside OPTIC; IST imitates 1ST.
explanation.definitionFit: An optimistic person looks on the bright side and expects good outcomes.

clue.text: Soon reversed electronic loop

indicators.note: reversed says the word soon is written backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A circuit loop that will shortly be reversed by electronics.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot.

clue.text: A bird name not applicable in Italy

definitions.note: a place in Italy, a noun phrase for a city there

parts.note: a raven is a large black bird
NA is the abbreviation for not applicable on forms

explanation.surface: A form in Italy asking for a bird's name, marked not applicable.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravenna is a city in north-east Italy famous for its mosaics.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravenna is a city of the Emilia-Romagna region in northern Italy.

clue.text: Cordelia's sister, almost majestic by name

indicators.note: almost signals the word for majestic stops short of its last letter

parts.note: regal means kingly or majestic

explanation.surface: A princess nearly as grand as her family name suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: In King Lear, Cordelia's sisters are Goneril and Regan.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is one of King Lear's two elder daughters in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Sing of one's ups and downs?

definitions.text: Sing of one's ups and downs?

parts.words: Sing of one's ups and downs?
parts.note: the voice leaping up and down between registers, as in Alpine song

explanation.surface: Singing about the highs and lows of one's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ups and downs' seems to mean fortunes, but describes the voice flipping between high and low notes, as in Alpine mountain song.
explanation.definitionFit: To yodel is to sing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Wager it's a letter from Greece

parts.note: a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A bettor remarking that a letter from Greece is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Nine reported to be in the desert

indicators.note: reported means the answer to clue nine is spoken

parts.note: the solution to clue 9 across, a small fish

explanation.surface: Nine people said to be stranded in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nine' is not a number but the answer to 9 across, a fish name that 'reported' turns into a spoken likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the vast desert spanning Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Award for an old injury

parts.note: a scar is the mark of an injury

explanation.surface: An honour granted to compensate for an old wound.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the statuette given at the Academy Awards for film.

clue.text: Figure-of-eight?

parts.note: a geometric figure with eight sides, not the looping shape of a numeral

explanation.surface: A reference to the looping figure-of-eight shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure-of-eight' suggests a looped shape like the number 8, but means a figure with eight sides.
explanation.definitionFit: An octagon is a polygon with eight sides and eight angles.

clue.text: It's strong, a Kenyan coffee

parts.note: robust means strong and sturdy

explanation.surface: A drinker praising a strong Kenyan brew.
explanation.definitionFit: Robusta is a hardy coffee species grown widely in Africa, Kenya included.

clue.text: In Rome, you can contrive to have a love-affair!

indicators.note: to contrive is to devise or rearrange, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A tourist told that Rome is the place to engineer a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrive' rearranges ROME and CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is an amorous relationship, a synonym of an affair of the heart.

clue.text: Do manic contortions, being unsettled

indicators.note: contortions are twistings, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Wild gyrations by someone feeling restless.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people wander without a fixed home, so they are not settled anywhere.

clue.text: In Malta, I chat in such a language? Unlikely

indicators.note: in tells us the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Wondering whether chatting in Malta would be done in this tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unlikely' is surface comment: an Altaic language, such as Turkish or Mongolian, would be odd to hear in Malta.
explanation.definitionFit: Altaic is a proposed family of Central Asian languages including Turkic and Mongolic.

clue.text: Almost insulated in an apartment house in old Rome

definitions.text: an apartment house in old Rome

indicators.note: almost means the word insulated stops short of its full length

explanation.surface: A Roman apartment block that is nearly soundproofed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the ending TED from INSULATED.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome an insula was a multi-storey tenement block.

clue.text: A Roman censor caught at love-making!

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A stern Roman moral guardian caught in the act of love.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder was a famously strict Roman censor, so catching him at love-making is comic.
explanation.definitionFit: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor and was known for moral severity.

clue.text: One usually gets two or eleven at bingo

definitions.text: One usually gets two or eleven at bingo

parts.words: One usually gets two or eleven at bingo
parts.note: a person normally has two limbs to walk on, and the bingo call for eleven pairs them with that number

explanation.surface: Musing on how many a player wins at bingo.
explanation.walkthrough: In British bingo, the caller announces 11 as 'legs eleven', because the digits look like two legs.
explanation.definitionFit: People normally have two lower limbs, and the bingo call for eleven uses the same word.

clue.text: It will help smooth things over

definitions.text: It will help smooth things over

parts.words: It will help smooth things over
parts.note: smoothing things over literally, rubbing a rough surface flat, rather than calming a quarrel

explanation.surface: A peacemaker offering something to calm a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smooth things over' suggests settling a dispute, but means sanding a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasspaper is an abrasive sheet coated with powdered glass, used for sanding wood.

clue.text: "Intolerance", the first entertaining picture of this type?

indicators.note: the first signals the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: Asking whether Intolerance was the first entertaining film of its genre.
explanation.walkthrough: Intolerance (1916) is D. W. Griffith's vast silent film, an example of the genre; the definition works by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerance is a huge silent film of grand scale, an example of a lavish historical spectacle.

clue.text: Face it — son's a twisted Nazi!

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of the preceding words are bent into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the S counting as a letter

explanation.surface: Telling someone to face the fact that their son has become a warped extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges FACE IT and SONS.
explanation.definitionFit: A neo-Nazi is a modern follower of fascism, so the far-right label matches.
